text:
maria (support): Hey team — customer reports the payment UI gets stuck on "processing" and then shows "Payment failed. Try again.". They pasted this response header: `x-request-id: req_9b2f4c` and said the browser console shows a 502 from `POST /v1/charges`.
devin (frontend): Thanks — can you get a HAR + console logs from their browser? quickest repro is ideal (steps + account). Also ask them to copy the network request as cURL so we can replay server-side.
maria (support): Repro steps I have so far: 1) login as test user 2) open /billing/checkout 3) enter card (test) 4) click pay -> spinner then modal error. Customer is on Chrome 121 on macOS 13. They attached a screenshot and the `x-request-id` above.
devin (frontend): Ok here's the exact instructions to send to customer — short and explicit.

1) Open Chrome DevTools: Menu > More tools > Developer tools (or F12)
2) Console: Click the Console tab, reproduce the issue, then right-click inside Console and choose "Save as..." to export logs (or copy visible messages).
3) Network: Click Network tab -> check "Preserve log" -> hit the Pay button to reproduce -> locate the failing `POST /v1/charges` request -> right-click the request -> "Save all as HAR with content" (or "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL (bash)").
4) In the HAR: please redact any full card numbers, and replace any `Authorization` header value with `REDACTED_AUTH` before sharing. Also remove cookies that look like `session=` or `__Secure-`.

Example of a safe curl to paste (replace tokens):
```
curl 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/charges' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: REDACTED_AUTH' \
  --data-raw '{"amount":1000,"currency":"usd","payment_method":"pm_test"}' \
  --compressed
```

If they can attach the HAR file to the ticket or upload to the support channel, that helps a lot.

raj (infra): Also ask them for the exact timestamp (local time) when they hit Pay, and confirm the `x-request-id`. I'll search logs. If they can't share HAR, the `Copy as cURL` is most useful.
devin (frontend): Additional notes for customers who are uneasy about sharing: they can remove the `request headers` > `cookie` and `authorization` fields in the HAR JSON before uploading, or send the HAR to us via the secure support upload link instead of pasting publicly.
maria (support): I'll send those steps now. Also asking them to include: account id/email, browser version, OS, exact reproduction steps, local time of repro, and whether they were on a VPN.
sre-bot: [incident tag] linked_incident:INC-2026-847 created for x-request-id req_9b2f4c — assigned to infra oncall.

raj (infra): Found server side trace for req_9b2f4c — it shows a backend timeout contacting the payment gateway at 2026-03-15T18:12:07Z. If they can provide the HAR we can confirm client payload and headers.
devin (frontend): If the customer can paste the `Copy as cURL` output, we can immediately run it from our network (with Authorization REDACTED) to reproduce the 502. If it reproduces, we capture a server-side full trace and correlate.
maria (support): Customer uploaded HAR to the ticket. They redacted Authorization and cookies and included console log file. Attaching here for triage.
devin (frontend): Perfect — I'll pull the HAR and cURL and try a repro locally. Quick checklist for us before requesting more from customer: 1) confirm exact request body 2) confirm request headers 3) confirm response code and response body in HAR 4) server-side trace for req_9b2f4c.

raj (infra): On it. If anyone needs to fetch logs by request id: internal command `rlogs --request req_9b2f4c` (internal-only). Will paste truncated stack/timeout info here once pulled.
maria (support): Thanks all, I'll keep customer updated with ETA and ask them not to clear their network tab until we confirm.
devin (frontend): One last tip for customers: if they use `Copy as cURL`, ask them to change `--compressed` to `--compressed --insecure` only if they hit TLS cert issues in their environment. Otherwise leave as-is.
maria (support): Ack, thanks. I'll follow up in the ticket with the HAR and the steps we ran. :thumbsup:
